[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#584-589)#### pub fn [noise_threshold](https://docs.rs#method.noise_threshold)(self, threshold: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)<M>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#584-589)

#### pub fn [noise_threshold](https://docs.rs#method.noise_threshold)(self, threshold: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)<M>

Changes the default noise threshold for benchmarks run with this runner. The noise threshold is used to filter out small changes in performance, even if they are statistically significant. Sometimes benchmarking the same code twice will result in small but statistically significant differences solely because of noise. This provides a way to filter out some of these false positives at the cost of making it harder to detect small changes to the true performance of the benchmark.

The default is 0.01, meaning that changes smaller than 1% will be ignored.

Panics if the threshold is set to a negative value

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#599-607)#### pub fn [confidence_level](https://docs.rs#method.confidence_level)(self, cl: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)<M>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#599-607)

#### pub fn [confidence_level](https://docs.rs#method.confidence_level)(self, cl: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)<M>

Changes the default confidence level for benchmarks run with this runner. The confidence
level is the desired probability that the true runtime lies within the estimated
[confidence interval](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confidence_interval). The default is
0.95, meaning that the confidence interval should capture the true value 95% of the time.

Panics if the confidence level is set to a value outside the `(0, 1)` range

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#629-634)#### pub fn [significance_level](https://docs.rs#method.significance_level)(self, sl: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)<M>

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#629-634)

#### pub fn [significance_level](https://docs.rs#method.significance_level)(self, sl: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)) -> [Criterion](https://docs.rs/struct.Criterion.html)<M>

Changes the default [significance level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_significance)
for benchmarks run with this runner. This is used to perform a
[hypothesis test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_hypothesis_testing) to see if
the measurements from this run are different from the measured performance of the last run.
The significance level is the desired probability that two measurements of identical code
will be considered ‘different’ due to noise in the measurements. The default value is 0.05,
meaning that approximately 5% of identical benchmarks will register as different due to
noise.

This presents a trade-off. By setting the significance level closer to 0.0, you can increase the statistical robustness against noise, but it also weakens Criterion.rs’ ability to detect small but real changes in the performance. By setting the significance level closer to 1.0, Criterion.rs will be more able to detect small true changes, but will also report more spurious differences.

See also the noise threshold setting.

Panics if the significance level is set to a value outside the `(0, 1)` range

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#656-660)No longer useful; since the plotters backend is available Criterion.rs can always generate plots

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#1099-1109)#### pub fn [benchmark_group](https://docs.rs#method.benchmark_group)<S: [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>(

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#1099-1109)

#### pub fn [benchmark_group](https://docs.rs#method.benchmark_group)<S: [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>>(

    &mut self,

    group_name: S

) -> [BenchmarkGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.BenchmarkGroup.html)<'_, M>

Return a benchmark group. All benchmarks performed using a benchmark group will be grouped together in the final report.

```
#[macro_use] extern crate criterion;
use self::criterion::*;
fn bench_simple(c: &mut Criterion) {
    let mut group = c.benchmark_group("My Group");
    // Now we can perform benchmarks with this group
    group.bench_function("Bench 1", |b| b.iter(|| 1 ));
    group.bench_function("Bench 2", |b| b.iter(|| 2 ));

    group.finish();
}
criterion_group!(benches, bench_simple);
criterion_main!(benches);
```
Panics if the group name is empty

#[macro_use] extern crate criterion;

fn bench(c: &mut Criterion) {
    // Setup (construct data, allocate memory, etc)
    c.bench_function(
        "function_name",
        |b| b.iter(|| {
            // Code to benchmark goes here
        }),
    );
}
criterion_group!(benches, bench);
criterion_main!(benches);
```

    F: [FnMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnMut.html)(&mut [Bencher](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html)<'_, M>, [&](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html)I),

Benchmarks a function with an input. For comparing multiple functions or multiple inputs,
see `benchmark_group`.

```
#[macro_use] extern crate criterion;
use self::criterion::*;
fn bench(c: &mut Criterion) {
    // Setup (construct data, allocate memory, etc)
    let input = 5u64;
    c.bench_with_input(
        BenchmarkId::new("function_name", input), &input,
        |b, i| b.iter(|| {
            // Code to benchmark using input `i` goes here
        }),
    );
}
criterion_group!(benches, bench);
criterion_main!(benches);
```
Creates a benchmark manager with the following default settings:

- Sample size: 100 measurements
- Warm-up time: 3 s
- Measurement time: 5 s
- Bootstrap size: 100 000 resamples
- Noise threshold: 0.01 (1%)
- Confidence level: 0.95
- Significance level: 0.05
- Plotting: enabled, using gnuplot if available or plotters if gnuplot is not available
- No filter

# PlotConfiguration in criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.3/struct.PlotConfiguration.html

`pub struct PlotConfiguration { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Contains the configuration options for the plots generated by a particular benchmark or benchmark group.

```
use self::criterion::{Bencher, Criterion, Benchmark, PlotConfiguration, AxisScale};
let plot_config = PlotConfiguration::default()
    .summary_scale(AxisScale::Logarithmic);
// Using Criterion::default() for simplicity; normally you'd use the macros.
let mut criterion = Criterion::default();
let mut benchmark_group = criterion.benchmark_group("Group name");
benchmark_group.plot_config(plot_config);
// Use benchmark group
```
[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#1394-1397)#### pub fn [summary_scale](https://docs.rs#method.summary_scale)(self, new_scale: [AxisScale](https://docs.rs/enum.AxisScale.html)) -> [PlotConfiguration](https://docs.rs/struct.PlotConfiguration.html)

Set the axis scale (linear or logarithmic) for the summary plots. Typically, you would set this to logarithmic if benchmarking over a range of inputs which scale exponentially. Defaults to linear.

# Baseline in criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.3/enum.Baseline.html

```
pub enum Baseline {
    Compare,
    Save,
}
```

## Expand description

Baseline describes how the baseline_directory is handled.

Compare ensures a previous saved version of the baseline
exists and runs comparison against that.

Save writes the benchmark results to the baseline directory,
overwriting any results that were previously there.

Performs copy-assignment from `source`. [Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#method.clone_from)

Formats the value using the given formatter. [Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Debug.html#tymethod.fmt)

Immutably borrows from an owned value. [Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.Borrow.html#tymethod.borrow)

Mutably borrows from an owned value. [Read more](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/borrow/trait.BorrowMut.html#tymethod.borrow_mut)

Returns the argument unchanged.

Calls `U::from(self)`.

That is, this conversion is whatever the implementation of
[From](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html)<T> for U

The alignment of pointer.

# BatchSize in criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.3/enum.BatchSize.html

## Expand description

Argument to [ Bencher::iter_batched](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.iter_batched) and

[which controls the batch size.](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.iter_batched_ref)

`Bencher::iter_batched_ref`Generally speaking, almost all benchmarks should use `SmallInput`. If the input or the result
of the benchmark routine is large enough that `SmallInput` causes out-of-memory errors,
`LargeInput` can be used to reduce memory usage at the cost of increasing the measurement
overhead. If the input or the result is extremely large (or if it holds some
limited external resource like a file handle), `PerIteration` will set the number of iterations
per batch to exactly one. `PerIteration` can increase the measurement overhead substantially
and should be avoided wherever possible.

Each value lists an estimate of the measurement overhead. This is intended as a rough guide to assist in choosing an option, it should not be relied upon. In particular, it is not valid to subtract the listed overhead from the measurement and assume that the result represents the true runtime of a function. The actual measurement overhead for your specific benchmark depends on the details of the function you’re benchmarking and the hardware and operating system running the benchmark.

With that said, if the runtime of your function is small relative to the measurement overhead
it will be difficult to take accurate measurements. In this situation, the best option is to use
[ Bencher::iter](https://docs.rs/struct.Bencher.html#method.iter) which has next-to-zero measurement overhead.

`SmallInput` indicates that the input to the benchmark routine (the value returned from
the setup routine) is small enough that millions of values can be safely held in memory.
Always prefer `SmallInput` unless the benchmark is using too much memory.

In testing, the maximum measurement overhead from benchmarking with `SmallInput` is on the
order of 500 picoseconds. This is presented as a rough guide; your results may vary.

`LargeInput` indicates that the input to the benchmark routine or the value returned from
that routine is large. This will reduce the memory usage but increase the measurement
overhead.

In testing, the maximum measurement overhead from benchmarking with `LargeInput` is on the
order of 750 picoseconds. This is presented as a rough guide; your results may vary.

`PerIteration` indicates that the input to the benchmark routine or the value returned from
that routine is extremely large or holds some limited resource, such that holding many values
in memory at once is infeasible. This provides the worst measurement overhead, but the
lowest memory usage.

In testing, the maximum measurement overhead from benchmarking with `PerIteration` is on the
order of 350 nanoseconds or 350,000 picoseconds. This is presented as a rough guide; your
results may vary.

`NumBatches(`[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

`NumBatches` will attempt to divide the iterations up into a given number of batches.
A larger number of batches (and thus smaller batches) will reduce memory usage but increase
measurement overhead. This allows the user to choose their own tradeoff between memory usage
and measurement overhead, but care must be taken in tuning the number of batches. Most
benchmarks should use `SmallInput` or `LargeInput` instead.

`NumIterations(`[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

`NumIterations` fixes the batch size to a constant number, specified by the user. This
allows the user to choose their own tradeoff between overhead and memory usage, but care must
be taken in tuning the batch size. In general, the measurement overhead of `NumIterations`
will be larger than that of `NumBatches`. Most benchmarks should use `SmallInput` or
`LargeInput` instead.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#232)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#232)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#232)

### impl [StructuralEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.StructuralEq.html) for [BatchSize](https://docs.rs/enum.BatchSize.html)

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#232)

# SamplingMode in criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.3/enum.SamplingMode.html

```
pub enum SamplingMode {
    Auto,
    Linear,
    Flat,
}
```
## Expand description

This enum allows the user to control how Criterion.rs chooses the iteration count when sampling. The default is Auto, which will choose a method automatically based on the iteration time during the warm-up phase.

Criterion.rs should choose a sampling method automatically. This is the default, and is recommended for most users and most benchmarks.

Scale the iteration count in each sample linearly. This is suitable for most benchmarks, but it tends to require many iterations which can make it very slow for very long benchmarks.

Keep the iteration count the same for all samples. This is not recommended, as it affects the statistics that Criterion.rs can compute. However, it requires fewer iterations than the Linear method and therefore is more suitable for very long-running benchmarks where benchmark execution time is more of a problem and statistical precision is less important.

---

# Throughput in criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.3/enum.Throughput.html

## Expand description

Enum representing different ways of measuring the throughput of benchmarked code. If the throughput setting is configured for a benchmark then the estimated throughput will be reported as well as the time per iteration.

`Bytes(`[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

Measure throughput in terms of bytes/second. The value should be the number of bytes
processed by one iteration of the benchmarked code. Typically, this would be the length of
an input string or `&[u8]`.

`Elements(`[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html))

Measure throughput in terms of elements/second. The value should be the number of elements processed by one iteration of the benchmarked code. Typically, this would be the size of a collection, but could also be the number of lines of input text or the number of values to parse.

[source](https://docs.rs/src/criterion/lib.rs.html#1338)

# black_box in criterion - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/criterion/^0.3/fn.black_box.html

`pub fn black_box<T>(dummy: T) -> T`## Expand description

A function that is opaque to the optimizer, used to prevent the compiler from optimizing away computations in a benchmark.

This variant is stable-compatible, but it may cause some performance overhead or fail to prevent code from being eliminated.

# lib.rs - source

# mime_guess/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)//! Guessing of MIME types by file extension.
[2](https://docs.rs#2)//!
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! Uses a static list of file-extension : MIME type mappings.
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! ```
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! # extern crate mime;
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! // the file doesn't have to exist, it just looks at the path
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! let guess = mime_guess::from_path("some_file.gif");
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//! assert_eq!(guess.first(), Some(mime::IMAGE_GIF));
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//!
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//! ```
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//!
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//! #### Note: MIME Types Returned Are Not Stable/Guaranteed
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//! The media types returned for a given extension are not considered to be part of the crate's
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//! stable API and are often updated in patch <br /> (`x.y.[z + 1]`) releases to be as correct as
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//! possible.
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//!
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//! Additionally, only the extensions of paths/filenames are inspected in order to guess the MIME
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! type. The file that may or may not reside at that path may or may not be a valid file of the
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//! returned MIME type.  Be wary of unsafe or un-validated assumptions about file structure or
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//! length.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)pub extern crate mime;
[23](https://docs.rs#23)extern crate unicase;
[24](https://docs.rs#24)

[40](https://docs.rs#40)/// A "guess" of the MIME/Media Type(s) of an extension or path as one or more
[41](https://docs.rs#41)/// [`Mime`](struct.Mime.html) instances.
[42](https://docs.rs#42)///
[43](https://docs.rs#43)/// ### Note: Ordering
[44](https://docs.rs#44)/// A given file format may have one or more applicable Media Types; in this case
[45](https://docs.rs#45)/// the first Media Type returned is whatever is declared in the latest IETF RFC for the
[46](https://docs.rs#46)/// presumed file format or the one that explicitly supercedes all others.
[47](https://docs.rs#47)/// Ordering of additional Media Types is arbitrary.
[48](https://docs.rs#48)///
[49](https://docs.rs#49)/// ### Note: Values Not Stable
[50](https://docs.rs#50)/// The exact Media Types returned in any given guess are not considered to be stable and are often
[51](https://docs.rs#51)/// updated in patch releases in order to reflect the most up-to-date information possible.
[52](https://docs.rs#52)#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[53](https://docs.rs#53)// FIXME: change repr when `mime` gains macro/const fn constructor
[54](https://docs.rs#54)pub struct MimeGuess(&'static [&'static str]);

[56](https://docs.rs#56)impl MimeGuess {
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    /// Guess the MIME type of a file (real or otherwise) with the given extension.
[58](https://docs.rs#58)    ///
[59](https://docs.rs#59)    /// The search is case-insensitive.
[60](https://docs.rs#60)    ///
[61](https://docs.rs#61)    /// If `ext` is empty or has no (currently) known MIME type mapping, then an empty guess is
[62](https://docs.rs#62)    /// returned.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)    pub fn from_ext(ext: &str) -> MimeGuess {
[64](https://docs.rs#64)        if ext.is_empty() {
[65](https://docs.rs#65)            return MimeGuess(&[]);
[66](https://docs.rs#66)        }
[67](https://docs.rs#67)
[68](https://docs.rs#68)        impl_::get_mime_types(ext).map_or(MimeGuess(&[]), |v| MimeGuess(v))
[69](https://docs.rs#69)    }
[70](https://docs.rs#70)
[71](https://docs.rs#71)    /// Guess the MIME type of `path` by its extension (as defined by
[72](https://docs.rs#72)    /// [`Path::extension()`]). **No disk access is performed.**
[73](https://docs.rs#73)    ///
[74](https://docs.rs#74)    /// If `path` has no extension, the extension cannot be converted to `str`, or has
[75](https://docs.rs#75)    /// no known MIME type mapping, then an empty guess is returned.
[76](https://docs.rs#76)    ///
[77](https://docs.rs#77)    /// The search is case-insensitive.
[78](https://docs.rs#78)    ///
[79](https://docs.rs#79)    /// ## Note
[80](https://docs.rs#80)    /// **Guess** is the operative word here, as there are no guarantees that the contents of the
[81](https://docs.rs#81)    /// file that `path` points to match the MIME type associated with the path's extension.
[82](https://docs.rs#82)    ///
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    /// Take care when processing files with assumptions based on the return value of this function.
[84](https://docs.rs#84)    ///
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    /// [`Path::extension()`]: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.extension
[86](https://docs.rs#86)    pub fn from_path<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> MimeGuess {
[87](https://docs.rs#87)        path.as_ref()
[88](https://docs.rs#88)            .extension()
[89](https://docs.rs#89)            .and_then(OsStr::to_str)
[90](https://docs.rs#90)            .map_or(MimeGuess(&[]), Self::from_ext)
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    }
[92](https://docs.rs#92)
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    /// `true` if the guess did not return any known mappings for the given path or extension.
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)        self.0.is_empty()
[96](https://docs.rs#96)    }
[97](https://docs.rs#97)
[98](https://docs.rs#98)    /// Get the number of MIME types in the current guess.
[99](https://docs.rs#99)    pub fn count(&self) -> usize {
[100](https://docs.rs#100)        self.0.len()
[101](https://docs.rs#101)    }
[102](https://docs.rs#102)
[103](https://docs.rs#103)    /// Get the first guessed `Mime`, if applicable.
[104](https://docs.rs#104)    ///
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    /// See [Note: Ordering](#note-ordering) above.
[106](https://docs.rs#106)    pub fn first(&self) -> Option<Mime> {
[107](https://docs.rs#107)        self.first_raw().map(expect_mime)
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    }
[109](https://docs.rs#109)
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    /// Get the first guessed Media Type as a string, if applicable.

[112](https://docs.rs#112)    /// See [Note: Ordering](#note-ordering) above.
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    pub fn first_raw(&self) -> Option<&'static str> {
[114](https://docs.rs#114)        self.0.get(0).cloned()
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    }
[116](https://docs.rs#116)
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    /// Get the first guessed `Mime`, or if the guess is empty, return
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    /// [`application/octet-stream`] instead.
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    ///
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    /// See [Note: Ordering](#note-ordering) above.
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    ///
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    /// ### Note: HTTP Applications
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    /// For HTTP request and response bodies if a value for the `Content-Type` header
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    /// cannot be determined it might be preferable to not send one at all instead of defaulting to
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    /// `application/octet-stream` as the recipient will expect to infer the format directly from
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    /// the content instead. ([RFC 7231, Section 3.1.1.5][rfc7231])
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    ///
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    /// On the contrary, for `multipart/form-data` bodies, the `Content-Type` of a form-data part is
[129](https://docs.rs#129)    /// assumed to be `text/plain` unless specified so a default of `application/octet-stream`
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    /// for non-text parts is safer. ([RFC 7578, Section 4.4][rfc7578])
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    ///
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    /// [`application/octet-stream`]: https://docs.rs/mime/0.3/mime/constant.APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM.html
[133](https://docs.rs#133)    /// [rfc7231]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-3.1.1.5
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    /// [rfc7578]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7578#section-4.4
[135](https://docs.rs#135)    pub fn first_or_octet_stream(&self) -> Mime {
[136](https://docs.rs#136)        self.first_or(mime::APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM)
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    }
[138](https://docs.rs#138)

[278](https://docs.rs#278)/// Guess the MIME type of `path` by its extension (as defined by `Path::extension()`).
[279](https://docs.rs#279)///
[280](https://docs.rs#280)/// If `path` has no extension, or its extension has no known MIME type mapping,
[281](https://docs.rs#281)/// then the MIME type is assumed to be `application/octet-stream`.
[282](https://docs.rs#282)///
[283](https://docs.rs#283)/// ## Note
[284](https://docs.rs#284)/// **Guess** is the operative word here, as there are no guarantees that the contents of the file
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// that `path` points to match the MIME type associated with the path's extension.
[286](https://docs.rs#286)///
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// Take care when processing files with assumptions based on the return value of this function.
[288](https://docs.rs#288)///
[289](https://docs.rs#289)/// In HTTP applications, it might be [preferable][rfc7231] to not send a `Content-Type`
[290](https://docs.rs#290)/// header at all instead of defaulting to `application/octet-stream`.
[291](https://docs.rs#291)///
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// [rfc7231]: https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-3.1.1.5
[293](https://docs.rs#293)#[deprecated(
[294](https://docs.rs#294)    since = "2.0.0",
[295](https://docs.rs#295)    note = "Use `from_path(path).first_or_octet_stream()` instead"
[296](https://docs.rs#296))]
[297](https://docs.rs#297)pub fn guess_mime_type<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Mime {
[298](https://docs.rs#298)    from_path(path).first_or_octet_stream()
[299](https://docs.rs#299)}
[300](https://docs.rs#300)

# Mime in mime_guess - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime_guess/latest/target-redirect/mime_guess/struct.Mime.html

`pub struct Mime { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A parsed mime or media type.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Get an optional +suffix for this `Mime`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-2)Example

```
let svg = "image/svg+xml".parse::<mime::Mime>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(svg.suffix(), Some(mime::XML));
assert_eq!(svg.suffix().unwrap(), "xml");
assert!(mime::TEXT_PLAIN.suffix().is_none());
```
Look up a parameter by name.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-3)Example

```
let mime = mime::TEXT_PLAIN_UTF_8;
assert_eq!(mime.get_param(mime::CHARSET), Some(mime::UTF_8));
assert_eq!(mime.get_param("charset").unwrap(), "utf-8");
assert!(mime.get_param("boundary").is_none());
let mime = "multipart/form-data; boundary=ABCDEFG".parse::<mime::Mime>().unwrap();
assert_eq!(mime.get_param(mime::BOUNDARY).unwrap(), "ABCDEFG");
```

# MimeGuess in mime_guess - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/mime_guess/latest/target-redirect/mime_guess/struct.MimeGuess.html

`pub struct MimeGuess(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A “guess” of the MIME/Media Type(s) of an extension or path as one or more
[ Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html) instances.

[§](https://docs.rs#note-ordering)Note: Ordering

A given file format may have one or more applicable Media Types; in this case the first Media Type returned is whatever is declared in the latest IETF RFC for the presumed file format or the one that explicitly supercedes all others. Ordering of additional Media Types is arbitrary.

[§](https://docs.rs#note-values-not-stable)Note: Values Not Stable

The exact Media Types returned in any given guess are not considered to be stable and are often updated in patch releases in order to reflect the most up-to-date information possible.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Guess the MIME type of a file (real or otherwise) with the given extension.

The search is case-insensitive.

If `ext` is empty or has no (currently) known MIME type mapping, then an empty guess is
returned.

Guess the MIME type of `path` by its extension (as defined by
[ Path::extension()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.extension)).

**No disk access is performed.**

If `path` has no extension, the extension cannot be converted to `str`, or has
no known MIME type mapping, then an empty guess is returned.

The search is case-insensitive.

[§](https://docs.rs#note)Note

**Guess** is the operative word here, as there are no guarantees that the contents of the
file that `path` points to match the MIME type associated with the path’s extension.

Take care when processing files with assumptions based on the return value of this function.

`true` if the guess did not return any known mappings for the given path or extension.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/mime_guess/lib.rs.html#135-137)#### pub fn [first_or_octet_stream](https://docs.rs#method.first_or_octet_stream)(&self) -> [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/mime_guess/lib.rs.html#135-137)

#### pub fn [first_or_octet_stream](https://docs.rs#method.first_or_octet_stream)(&self) -> [Mime](https://docs.rs/struct.Mime.html)

Get the first guessed `Mime`, or if the guess is empty, return
[ application/octet-stream](https://docs.rs/mime/0.3/mime/constant.APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM.html) instead.

See [Note: Ordering](https://docs.rs#note-ordering) above.

[§](https://docs.rs#note-http-applications)Note: HTTP Applications

For HTTP request and response bodies if a value for the `Content-Type` header
cannot be determined it might be preferable to not send one at all instead of defaulting to
`application/octet-stream` as the recipient will expect to infer the format directly from
the content instead. ([RFC 7231, Section 3.1.1.5](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-3.1.1.5))

On the contrary, for `multipart/form-data` bodies, the `Content-Type` of a form-data part is
assumed to be `text/plain` unless specified so a default of `application/octet-stream`
for non-text parts is safer. ([RFC 7578, Section 4.4](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7578#section-4.4))
